chunks: Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (al-Rida) (peace be upon him) that he said:

I asked him about what is slaughtered for other than Allah. He said: 'That which is slaughtered for an idol, or a statue, or a tree, Allah made forbidden, just as He forbade the carcass, blood, and pork.' [He quoted]: 'So whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him.' [To eat the carcass].

I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, when does the carcass become permissible for the one forced by necessity? He said: 'My father narrated to me from his father from their fathers (peace be upon them) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked, and it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, we are in a land where hunger strikes us, so when does the carcass become permissible for us? He said: 'Until you become satiated or become full or eat greens, then it is up to you [to avoid it].'

Abd al-Azim said: I said to him, O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of His Exalted Saying: 'So whoever is forced, neither desiring nor transgressing'? He said: 'The 'Adi (transgressor) is the thief, and the Bashi (one who seeks) is the one who seeks game out of arrogance and amusement, not to provide for his family. They are not permitted to eat the carcass if forced; it is forbidden for them in the state of necessity just as it is forbidden for them in the state of choice, and they are not permitted to shorten their fasting or prayer during travel.'

I said to him, and His Exalted Saying: 'And the strangled, and the beaten to death, and the fallen to death, and the gored, and what the wild animals have eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death]'? He said: 'The strangled is the one that strangled itself with its neck until it died. The beaten to death is the one that was sick and the illness struck it until there was no movement in it. The fallen to death is the one that falls from a high place to a lower one, or falls from a mountain or into a well, and dies. The gored is the one that is gored by another beast and dies. And what the wild animal ate from it and died, and what was slaughtered on the pillars, on a stone or on an idol, except what its slaughter was caught [i.e., it was still alive] and was slaughtered.'

I said, 'And that you consult by the arrows [of chance]?' He said: 'In the time of Ignorance, they would buy a camel among ten people and consult by arrows upon it. There were ten arrows: seven had shares (Nasib) and three had no shares. As for those with shares: Al-Fadh (the single), Al-Taw'am (the pair), An-Nafis (the valuable), Al-Hils (the covering), Al-Musbil (the drooping), Al-Mu'alla (the raised), and Ar-Raqib (the watchful). As for those with no shares: As-Safihi (the small), Al-Manih (the rejected), and Al-Waghdu (the mixed). They would mix the arrows among ten people. Whoever had an arrow drawn from the 'no share' group was obliged to pay one-third of the camel's price. They would continue like this until the 'no share' arrows fell to three, so they obliged them to pay the full price of the camel. Then they would slaughter it and the seven who did not pay anything for its price would eat it, and they did not feed the three who covered its price anything. When Islam came, Allah Exalted is His mention forbade that among what He forbade, and He said Exalted is He: 'And that you consult by the arrows, that is insolence.' Meaning: Forbidden.'

key_terms.أُدْرِكَتْ ذَكَاتُهُ: Its slaughter was caught (it was still alive when slaughtered)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and exceptions for eating a dead animal (maytah) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the jurisprudential boundaries of *dabt al-nadr* (necessity) by distinguishing between genuine survival needs and frivolous consumption, such as hunting for sport or theft. He further provides precise zoological definitions for the five categories of *Maytah* (dead meat) mentioned in the Quran and contextualizes the prohibition of *Al-Azlam* by detailing the specific pre-Islamic camel distribution mechanism that relied on chance rather than equitable contribution.
